description.narrative: Jordan is amongst the most water-scarce countries in the world, with large parts of the population receiving water intermittently. The situation is likely to be exacerbated by climate change and increase in population. By increasing the volume of available water resources and providing a continuous water supply, the Project is expected to increase the quality of water service and the quantity of the water consumed by households. The Project is expected to provide safe and reliable water to millions of Jordanians, meeting daily minimum water consumption recommendations, and enhancing their resilience to climate risks. The Project is also expected to create thousands of jobs. On the market side, the Project is expected to increase the resilience of both Jordans water sector and other key economic sectors, such as agriculture, to climate risks.

The Project involves the design, financing, construction, operation, and maintenance of a seawater desalination and conveyance system from Aqaba to Amman (including renewable power generation facilities) in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan. It comprises of (i) a marine intake and outfall system and large-scale desalination plant located in Aqaba, (ii) a 438-km conveyance pipeline delivering desalinated water from the desalination plant in Aqaba to the cities of Aqaba and Amman, and (iii) a c.280 MW solar PV plant to cover part of its energy needs. The AAWDCP will be developed under a Public-Private Partnership on a Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Maintain-Transfer (DBFOMT) basis pursuant to a 30-year concession agreement between the Government of Jordan and the private project company. Upon completion of the concession term, the Project assets will be transferred to the Government.
